panels.figure_caption: Left popliteal web with bifid scrotum, penoscrotal transposition, abnormal perineal mucosal patch, and foot anomaly
in_text_mentions: as flexed secondary to a tight popliteal web. The left foot had talipes equinovarus deformity with absence of 4th and 5th toes. Another toe was present behind the heel giving the appearance of a partial duplication of the foot. Penoscrotal transposition, bifid scrotum with bilateral descended testis, and proximal penile hypospadias were noted. A large mucosal patch was seen in the perineum on the left side [Figure 1]. The anal opening was normally located. The left kidney was not visualized on ultrasonography. Radiographs of the left lower limb showed normal long bones and a rotated calcaneum.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: 2D prenatal ultrasound showing popliteal pterygium web in fetus with article diagnosis of Popliteal Pterygium Syndrome; caption and in-text describe bilateral popliteal pterygia thigh to heels with knee extension restriction. B: 3D ultrasound reconstruction demonstrating popliteal webbing in same PPS fetus; directly captioned as popliteal webbing. C: Prenatal ultrasound of club foot described as showing ectrodactyly; in-text reports bilateral talipes equinovarus, syndactyly and ectrodactyly of toes in PPS fetus. Syndactyly is vocab term; talipes and ectrodactyly proposed as not in vocabulary. D: Coronal fetal face ultrasound showing bilateral upper lip grooves, interpreted in-text as suspicious cleft lips in PPS case; supports cleft lip finding.
